# Grid

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

A layout grid: arranges content in weighted columns and aligned rows for visual layout — address blocks, totals boxes, forms, side-by-side panels — as opposed to tabular data.

`Grid` reuses `Table`'s column-weight, pagination, and cell engine (padding, borders, backgrounds, per-cell alignment), so it is the right tool when columns must stay aligned across multiple rows. What differs is meaning: a `Grid` is tagged in the PDF structure tree as a generic `Div` grouping, and each cell's content tags itself in reading order. It therefore carries no table semantics — no phantom "table with N columns" announced to assistive tech, and no PDF/UA §7.5 header requirement. It is accessible by construction.

Choosing the right element:

- A single row of columns (a key/value pair, a label + amount) → prefer `HorizontalStack` with `WidthDistribution.Weighted`; it is lighter.
- Multiple rows whose columns must line up (a form, an invoice details block, side-by-side panels) → `Grid`.
- Actual tabular data (rows and columns with header relationships) → `Table`, and mark its header cells so it emits `TH`.

`Grid` pins the layout-grid tagging on, so — unlike `Presentation` — it can never be flipped back into a data table by mistake.

Namespace `BonniePDF`. Extends `Table`.

## Constructors

```csharp
new Grid(params float[] columnWeights)
```
